source.title: Domain-Specificity of Refusal Representations in Large Language Models

page_placements.theme: Category and topic structure: shared refusal component, category-specific harm parts, topic-specific (political) refusal

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests refusal-direction ablation and cross-domain effects, but extracts directions using a domain-specific PCA component rather than the original difference-in-means method.
record.gate_note: The study reports refusal rates after ablation, baseline refusal rates, direction-similarity measures, and a qualitative activation-visualization result. It also describes the layer sweep, random-direction control, and strength sweep. No result is reported for adding the direction, harmless-request refusal after addition, or general capability preservation. The individual cells of the cross-domain heatmap are not given in the text.
record.test_reason: The study ablates a harmful-vs-harmless refusal direction in Llama 3.1 8B Instruct and reports refusal rates against the unablated baseline and a random-direction control. That bears directly on V1's ablation claim. The direction comes from a PCA component rather than difference-in-means, so this is T2, not T1. Its main question, domain invariance, fits no listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that refusal directions are domain-invariant, citing three lines of evidence: statistically indistinguishable cross-domain ablation, high cosine similarity, and t-SNE clustering. They argue the single direction is 'not an aggregate artifact' and frame it as a systemic vulnerability. They suggest future alignment encode refusal through multiple mechanisms, and they note the single-architecture limit.
record.recipe_differences: Inspired by the original workflow and uses projection ablation, but identifies each domain's direction as a PCA component separating harmful from harmless activations rather than the original difference-in-means direction. It tests cross-domain ablation at several strengths and includes random-direction and layer-sweep validations.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome patterns varied by domain pairing: programming ablation had a within-domain advantage, while writing ablation showed the reverse. The strength sweep from α = 0.5 to 2.0 showed no consistent domain-specific pattern; at higher strengths cross-domain ablation was slightly more effective. The layer sweep reported 25-point reductions for layers 8 and 10.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal directions extracted per task domain (programming, scientific, writing) are geometrically similar and align with a universal direction. Cross-domain ablation reduces refusal about as much as within-domain ablation (p=0.324), with an inconsistent pattern across domain pairings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction is shared across task domains: one domain's direction reduces refusal in other domains.

record.problems: The test set contains only 15 prompts per domain, and the study tests only Llama 3.1 8B Instruct. The reported programming-versus-writing within/cross-domain pattern is inconsistent. The Fisher's exact test gives p = 0.324, and the text cautions that failure to reject the null does not prove universality. No general-capability check is reported; individual heatmap cell values are not provided in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The Figure 1 heatmap's individual cross-domain cells are not transcribed in the text, so no separate rows were created for those figure-only cells. No other reported applicable numerical outcomes were left out.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; refusal on harmless prompts after ablation; preservation of general capabilities; the difference-in-means extraction; models other than Llama 3.1 8B Instruct.
All parts. No weight edit is evaluated, despite the methods text mentioning weight modification.
Languages, model variants and base-to-instruct transfer are not tested; only task domains are.

missing.what: Individual cells of the cross-domain ablation heatmap, including scientific-direction results
Per-alpha refusal rates for alpha 0.5, 1.5 and 2.0
Layer-sweep results for layers other than 8 and 10
Layer-wise cosine similarity values (layer 8: 0.604, layer 12: 0.813, layer 31: 0.673) and UMAP results

record.verdict_notes: Ablation here is inference-time projection subtraction, though the methods text describes a weight modification; no weight edit is evaluated. The direction is a PCA component, not difference-in-means. The test set is 15 prompts per domain. The random-direction control's large effect (about 89% down to 50–65%) weakens any causal specificity. Capability is not checked, and the induction (addition) half of V1 is not tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction, inducing refusal on harmless requests, preservation of general capability, or the exact difference-in-means extraction method. It does not establish ablation at every layer and position or test additional models.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Does not test affine, cone, or dominant-direction-plus-others accounts of refusal.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Tests transfer across task domains, not across languages, model variants, or from base to instruct models.
Does not vary refusal-training procedures or training stages.

relation.reason: Reports its own refusal rates after ablation against the unablated baseline and a random-direction control.

tranche.reason: Asks the same causal question (does ablating a harmful-vs-harmless direction reduce refusal) with a different method: a PCA component, inference-time projection scaled by alpha, and a Claude judge.

source_check.notes: This is a 2-page FLAIRS abstract with 15 harmful prompts per domain. Several rates (10.0%, 28.3%, 25.6%) are not multiples of 1/15, so they may be averaged over something the text doesn't state. The domain-invariance result (cross-domain ablation, cosine 0.758 task-to-task and 0.916 to universal) may bear on V4 (single vs. several directions) more than on V1; consider a V4 link. Capabilities and activation addition were not tested. The scientific-domain ablation values appear only in the Figure 1 heatmap.

statements.correction: Within-domain average 25.6% vs. cross-domain 32.2% at alpha=1.0; Fisher's exact p=0.324. Task-to-universal cosine mean 0.916 (σ=0.029); task-to-task mean 0.758. Per-domain pattern inconsistent: programming 10.0% within vs. 36.7% cross; writing 40.0% within vs. 28.3% cross.
statements.problem: The content is right. The cited rows don't carry its numbers: p=0.324 compares the averages in R9 and R10, not R6. The universal alignment is the task-to-universal mean of 0.916, not R15's task-to-task 0.758.
